title: [Audit] API key inventory
description: One row per API key seen in range, busiest first (up to 1,000), Cloud and Elasticsearch keys, with owner and first and last use. A re-issued key keeps its name under a new id, so a name can repeat.
esql: SET unmapped_fields="nullify"; FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE api_key.id IS NOT NULL OR user.domain == "_cloud_api_key" | STATS events = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(client.ip), indices = COUNT_DISTINCT(elasticsearch.audit.indices) BY api_key.name, api_key.id, user.email, user.name | EVAL key_id = COALESCE(api_key.id, user.name), api_key = COALESCE(api_key.name, CASE((LENGTH(user.name) == 20 AND user.name RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT user.name RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(user.name, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), "(no name)")), owner = CASE(api_key.id IS NULL, "Cloud organization", COALESCE(user.email, CASE((LENGTH(user.name) == 20 AND user.name RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT user.name RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(user.name, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), user.name), "not recorded")) | KEEP api_key, key_id, owner, first_seen, last_seen, events, ips, indices | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 1000 | RENAME api_key AS `API key`, key_id AS `Key ID`, owner AS Owner, first_seen AS `First seen`, last_seen AS `Last seen`, events AS Events, ips AS IPs, indices AS Indices
